QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_42

question.text: Latika invests all her money exclusively in equities. During a market downturn, she finds that the value of her entire portfolio has declined significantly. What investment principle should Latika have followed to reduce this risk?

answer.text: Diversification across asset classes including debt, gold, and real estate
Investing everything in a single large-cap stock instead
Timing the market perfectly by selling before every downturn
Borrowing additional funds to invest more in equities during the downturn

explanation.text: The Logic: Latika's portfolio is concentrated in a single asset class — equity — so a downturn in equity markets affects the entire portfolio. Diversification across equity, debt, gold, and real estate can cushion the impact because these asset classes do not all move together. The Trap: Concentrating into a single stock (option B) increases concentration risk further. Perfectly timing the market (option C) is not a reliable strategy. Borrowing to invest more during a downturn (option D) amplifies losses if prices fall further. Note: Asset allocation across non-correlated or less-correlated asset classes is the source-supported response to concentration risk illustrated by the Latika example.
